title: Jain Philosophy: Many-Sided Truth and Non-Violence

questions.question: How many Tirthankaras does Jain tradition count, and who was the last?
questions.rationale: There are 24 ford-makers: Rishabhanatha (Adinatha) first, Parshvanatha 23rd, and Mahavira (540–468 BCE, traditional dates) the 24th.

questions.question: Which vow did Mahavira add to the four taught by Parshvanatha?
questions.rationale: Parshvanatha's four restraints were ahimsa, satya, asteya, and aparigraha; Mahavira added brahmacharya (celibacy) as the fifth great vow.

questions.question: Anekantavada — the doctrine of many-sidedness — implies that:
options: There is no truth at all
Every judgement is made from a partial standpoint, so no single statement captures reality whole
questions.rationale: Reality has infinitely many aspects (anekanta), and each claim reflects a partial standpoint (naya) — as in the blind men and the elephant parable.

questions.question: The word 'syat' in Jain syadvada means:
questions.rationale: Each of the seven predications is qualified by 'syat' — in some respect — marking the partial standpoint from which the claim holds.

questions.question: In Jain metaphysics, karma is:
options: Literal, subtle matter (pudgala) that flows into and binds the soul
questions.rationale: Jainism uniquely treats karma as physical matter that binds the soul — asrava is its inflow, bandha its sticking, nirjara its shedding.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT among the seven tattvas?
questions.rationale: The seven tattvas are jiva, ajiva, asrava (influx), bandha (bondage), samvara (stoppage), nirjara (shedding), and moksha. Prakriti belongs to Samkhya.

questions.question: How does the Jain view of the soul differ from the Buddhist?
options: Jains deny any soul; Buddhists affirm it
For Jains the soul is a real, conscious agent; Buddhists find no permanent self
Both affirm an eternal, unchanging self
questions.rationale: The Jain jiva acts, enjoys, and suffers eternally; the Buddhist anatta doctrine finds only a stream of aggregates and no permanent self.

questions.question: The Jain practice of sweeping the ground and straining water before use reflects which vow, taken to its extreme?
questions.rationale: Jain ahimsa extends to all living beings — monks sweep the path and strain water to avoid harming even insects, stricter than any parallel tradition.

questions.question: The Jain ratnatraya (three jewels) consists of:
options: Right faith, right knowledge, right conduct
questions.rationale: The Jain three jewels are qualities of the seeker — samyak darshana, jnana, and charitra. Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha is the Buddhist Triratna.

questions.question: The Digambara and Svetambara sects differ over:
options: Whether monks go naked or wear white robes
questions.rationale: Digambara ('sky-clad') monks wear nothing; Svetambara ('white-clad') monks wear white robes. The Agama canon was compiled at Pataliputra around 300 BCE under Sthulabhadra.
